header.name: Advanced Topics in Partial Differential Equations
header.description: This course is designed for senior undergraduate and Ph.D. students to explore advanced theoretical concepts in Partial Differential Equations (PDEs), focusing on non-linear PDEs, variational methods, regularity theory, and applications in physics and geometry.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Analyze and evaluate advanced concepts in PDEs theory, including their applications in complex problem-solving contexts.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Employ variational methods to solve complex PDEs.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Analyze and integrate the connections between PDEs, geometry, and physics, and evaluate the implications of these connections for modeling and solving complex problems in applied mathematics.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Critically evaluate recent research literature in PDEs.

lecture_topics: Introduction to PDEs and Nonlinear Problems: Basic concepts of PDEs
classification
initial and boundary value problems
review of linear PDEs
introduction to common nonlinear PDEs
methods for solving first-order nonlinear PDEs (e.g., characteristics)
physical examples of nonlinear PDEs from fluid dynamics and materials science
Nonlinear PDEs: Existence and Uniqueness: Picard's method and fixed-point theorems
introduction to weak solutions and energy methods
applications in nonlinear diffusion equations
Sobolev Spaces I: Definition and Basic Properties: Introduction to Sobolev spaces Wk,p
embedding theorems
compactness results in Sobolev spaces
trace theorems
Sobolev inequalities
Sobolev Spaces II: Regularity Theory: Weak derivatives and their use in regularity results
regularity for elliptic PDEs including De Giorgi-Nash-Moser theorem
regularity in parabolic PDEs
Aronson-Bénilan estimates
Elliptic PDEs I: Linear Elliptic Equations: Strong maximum principle
Harnack inequality
Green's functions and their applications
examples of elliptic equations in physics including Laplace and Poisson equations
Elliptic PDEs II: Nonlinear Elliptic Equations: Introduction to nonlinear elliptic equations such as the Monge-Ampère equation
variational approach to elliptic equations
existence results via minimization and mountain pass lemma
Parabolic PDEs: Heat Equation and Diffusion: Fundamental solutions and properties of the heat equation
maximum principles for parabolic equations
regularity theory for parabolic equations
Variational Methods I: Fundamentals: Introduction to calculus of variations
Euler-Lagrange equations and boundary value problems
direct methods in the calculus of variations
Variational Methods II: Applications to PDEs: Applications of variational principles to elliptic PDEs
variational inequalities and obstacle problems
examples in fluid mechanics and elasticity
Free Boundary Problems I: Introduction: Motivation and examples including Stefan problem and Hele-Shaw problem
weak and classical solutions to free boundary problems
methods for solving free boundary problems
Free Boundary Problems II: Regularity and Analysis: Regularity of free boundaries
the obstacle problem and regularity of the free boundary
applications in phase transitions and fluid mechanics
Hyperbolic PDEs I: Wave Equation: Solutions of the wave equation in different dimensions
D'Alembert’s solution
spherical means
energy methods for the wave equation
Hyperbolic PDEs II: Nonlinear Wave Equations: Nonlinear hyperbolic PDEs
conservation laws
shock waves
characteristics
Riemann invariants
examples from gas dynamics and shallow water waves

L. Hörmander, "The Analysis of Linear Partial Differential Operators I-IV," Springer, 2003.
